extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, assignees, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria governing who may act as representative in U.S. patent applications and proceedings, how powers of attorney are granted/revoked, how correspondence and customer numbers are designated, and the procedural effects of those choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee revocation and appointment of power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignee of record of the entire interest can revoke the power of attorney of the applicant and appoint a new power of attorney (unless an irrevocable right to prosecute was given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A power of attorney by the assignee of the entire interest revokes all powers given by the applicant and prior assignees if the assignee establishes their right to take action as provided in 37 CFR 3.73(b). Form PTO/SB/80 may be used by an assignee of the entire interest to revoke a power of attorney and appoint a new power of attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may conduct prosecution (37 CFR 3.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee who becomes of record may conduct prosecution to the exclusion of the inventive entity or previous assignees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible prosecuting assignees: (1) a single assignee of the entire right, title and interest of record; or (2) partial assignees together or with inventors who together own the entire interest. A partial assignee has less than the entire right, title and interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becoming of record requirement (§3.73(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee becomes of record in an application or reexamination by filing a statement in compliance with §3.73(b) signed by a party authorized to act on behalf of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing the assignee's right to act (e.g., to revoke prior powers) requires compliance with §3.73(b); see MPEP §324 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of assignee taking action under 1.47(a) status
rubrics_metrics.description: In applications accorded status under 37 CFR 1.47(a), an assignee of the entire interest of the available inventors may revoke a power of attorney given by inventors who signed the declaration (available inventors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rights of the assignee to take action may be established as provided in 37 CFR 3.73(b) and MPEP §324; see 37 CFR 1.32(b)(4) for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on entering POA during interference by technical support staff
rubrics_metrics.description: While an application is involved in an interference, no power of attorney of any kind should be entered in such application by the technical support staff of the Technology Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a power of attorney or revocation is received for an application in interference, forward it to the Service Branch of the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences because all parties must be notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition for non-registered individuals (37 CFR 11.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual not registered under §11.6 may be given limited recognition to prosecute specified patent applications upon showing necessity/justification, good moral character, and reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is narrow in scope (only the specified applications), is not granted while examinees await registration, and special rules apply to nonimmigrant aliens (recognition tied to authorized employment/training and will expire on departure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation in international applications (37 CFR 1.455 and PCT rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants of international applications may be represented by attorneys/agents registered to practice before the USPTO or by a common representative; appointment revokes earlier appointments unless otherwise indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment must be effected in the Request form, Demand form, or in a separate power of attorney submitted to the U.S. Receiving Office or the International Bureau. Powers of attorney and revocations should be submitted to the U.S. Receiving Office until issuance of the international search report. See MPEP §1807 and applicable PCT rules (Art.49, Rules 4.8, 90).

rubrics_metrics.name: How appointment of agent/attorney/common representative must be effected
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointment must be effected either in the Request, in the Demand, or in a separate power of attorney submitted to the Receiving Office or International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appointment revokes any earlier appointment unless otherwise indicated (PCT Rule 90.6(b) and (c)); an attorney may appoint an associate who shall be of record (PCT Rule 90.1(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for papers giving/revoking power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers giving or revoking a power of attorney generally require signature by all the applicants or owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If signed by less than all applicants/owners, acceptance requires a petition under 37 CFR 1.36(a) and fee (revocation) showing sufficient cause, or a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 and fee (appointment) demonstrating extraordinary circumstances where justice requires waiver of 37 CFR 1.32(b)(4). Petition should be directed to the Office of Petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences when less-than-all applicants sign POA papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of papers signed by less than all applicants/owners (via petition) can result in more than one attorney, agent, applicant, or owner prosecuting the application at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore, each of those parties must sign all subsequent replies submitted to the Office; the Office will indicate who must sign subsequent replies and dual correspondence will still not be permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for applications under 37 CFR 1.47(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an application filed under 37 CFR 1.47(a), an assignee of the entire interest of the available inventors who have signed the declaration may appoint or revoke a power of attorney without a petition under 37 CFR 1.36(a) or 1.183.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, a petition under 37 CFR 1.36(a) or 1.183 by a previously nonsigning inventor who later joins will not be granted. See MPEP §§402.07 and 409.03(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of who must sign replies when multiple responsible parties exist
rubrics_metrics.description: If coinventor A has given a POA to a practitioner and coinventor B has not, replies must be signed by the patent practitioner of A and by coinventor B. If coinventors A and B each appointed their own practitioner, replies must be signed by both practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicit illustrations that acceptance of partial-signature POA papers creates multiple signatory obligations; each attorney/agent signing subsequent papers must indicate whom they represent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address requirement (37 CFR 1.33(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing an application, a correspondence address must be set forth in either an application data sheet (§1.76) or elsewhere in a clearly identifiable manner in any paper submitted with an application filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will direct all notices, official letters, and other communications to the correspondence address. If no correspondence address is specified, the Office may treat the mailing address of the first named inventor as the correspondence address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office will not undertake double correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not engage in double correspondence with an applicant and a patent practitioner, or with more than one patent practitioner except as deemed necessary by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where double correspondence is attempted, form paragraph 4.01 ('Dual Correspondence') should be included in the next Office action. The first time a direct reply from applicant is received, include paragraph 4.01 and send a copy of the action to applicant; subsequent direct replies may be handled differently (see Examiner Note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office selection of one correspondence address among multiples
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one correspondence address is specified, the Office will select one of the specified addresses for use as the correspondence address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order of preference: (A) application data sheet (ADS); (B) application transmittal; (C) oath or declaration (unless power of attorney is more current); and (D) power of attorney. If more than one correspondence address is specified in a single document, the Office will select the address associated with a Customer Number over a typed correspondence address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daytime telephone number submission
rubrics_metrics.description: For the party to whom correspondence is to be addressed, a daytime telephone number should be supplied in a clearly identifiable manner and may be changed by any party who may change the correspondence address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While written record governs (37 CFR 1.2), a telephone number is useful to initiate contact that could later be reduced to writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may change the correspondence address (before and after §1.63 filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to filing of a §1.63 oath/declaration, the correspondence address may be changed by the party who filed the application (or a named patent practitioner in transmittal papers). After a §1.63 oath/declaration has been filed, the correspondence address may be changed only by the parties set forth in §1.33(b) (with exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application was filed by a patent practitioner, any other patent practitioner named in the transmittal papers may also change the address prior to §1.63 filing. A company that files an application may designate/change the correspondence address until a 1.63 oath/declaration is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign amendments and other papers (37 CFR 1.33(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and other papers (except certain written assertions) filed in the application must be signed by: (1) a patent practitioner of record appointed under §1.32(b); (2) a patent practitioner not of record who acts under §1.34; (3) an assignee as provided under §3.71(b); or (4) all of the applicants, unless there is an assignee of the entire interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is an assignee of the entire interest who has taken action in accordance with §3.71, that assignee may sign without all applicants signing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination correspondence and signing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All notices, official letters, and other communications for the patent owner(s) in a reexamination proceeding will be directed to the attorney or agent of record; amendments and other papers must be signed by the patent owner(s) or the attorney/agent of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double correspondence with the patent owner(s) and their attorney/agent, or with more than one attorney/agent, will not be undertaken. If more than one attorney/agent is of record and no correspondence address specified, correspondence will be held with the last attorney/agent made of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee address vs correspondence address (Customer Number and §1.363)
rubrics_metrics.description: A correspondence address or change thereto may be filed during the enforceable life of the patent and will be used in any correspondence relating to maintenance fees unless a separate 'fee address' has been specified (§1.363).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation of a 'fee address' by reference to a Customer Number will cause maintenance fee correspondence to be sent to the Customer Number's address; other correspondence goes to the correspondence address Customer Number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers of attorney to firms not recognized
rubrics_metrics.description: Powers of attorney to firms are not recognized by the USPTO; the firm’s address may be used for the correspondence address but the appointment must name practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'In care of' formatting if using a firm address (example provided). Patent practitioners must separately update the roster (37 CFR 11.11) in addition to any change filed in individual patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Number may designate correspondence, fee address, and list practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: A Customer Number may be used to designate the correspondence address, designate the fee address, and submit a list of practitioners such that those practitioners associated with the Customer Number would have power of attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customer Number associated with correspondence address is used to obtain PAIR access. Forms suggested: PTO/SB/125 (request Customer Number), PTO/SB/124 (change data), PTO/SB/122 (change correspondence address application), PTO/SB/123 (change correspondence address patent). Electronic batch updates for power of attorney are no longer accepted (see Official Gazette notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of associating practitioners with a Customer Number
rubrics_metrics.description: Association of a list of practitioners with a Customer Number permits an applicant to appoint all practitioners associated with that Customer Number merely by reference to the Customer Number in the Power of Attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding/deleting a practitioner via PTO/SB/124 updates the list across affected applications and avoids filing additional papers in each application. Appointment of practitioners via Customer Number is optional; individual naming remains allowed if fewer than ten practitioners are named (37 CFR 1.32(c)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Number does not equate to appointment of a law firm
rubrics_metrics.description: The Customer Number practice does not permit appointment of a law firm (rather than specified practitioners) because the Office cannot verify association solely by firm name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will permit appointment of all practitioners associated with a Customer Number because the Office can verify association from its records for that Customer Number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution of inconsistencies involving Customer Number addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Customer Number is provided in an application and there are inconsistencies between addresses, such inconsistencies generally will be resolved in favor of the address of the Customer Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to prohibition against dual correspondence, an applicant is permitted to provide only a single Customer Number at a time as the correspondence address. Applicants are cautioned not to attempt to appoint more than one Customer Number for a particular purpose in a single communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: System limitations when both Customer Number and individual practitioners provided
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant appoints all practitioners associated with a Customer Number as well as a list of individually named practitioners, the action will be treated as only an appointment of all practitioners associated with the Customer Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office computer systems do not allow entry of both a power of attorney to practitioners associated with a Customer Number and a list of practitioners; this avoids confusion and data entry errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons authorized to change Customer Number information
rubrics_metrics.description: The persons authorized to change information associated with an established Customer Number are: (1) a registered practitioner associated with the Customer Number; and (2) the person who requested the Customer Number (signed the Request form PTO/SB/125).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to the Customer Number data (address or list of practitioners) are effected using PTO/SB/124; electronic batch updates are limited as described in official notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of filing without a correspondence address
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is filed without a correspondence address, the Office cannot notify the applicant to complete the application; the applicant is considered to have constructive notice and will have 2 months from the filing date to complete the application before abandonment occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nonprovisional applications missing fees/oath/declaration, the applicant will be notified and given time to file missing parts and pay surcharge if a correspondence address is available. Periods may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136; failure to complete in time will cause abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence held with associate attorney when principal-associate relation exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Where attorneys bear relation of principal attorney and associate attorney, correspondence will be had with the associate attorney unless the principal directs otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The associate attorney may specify or change the correspondence address to which communications about the application are to be directed. Note: associate powers of attorney are not accepted after June 25, 2004, but previously filed associate powers continue to have effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple principal patent practitioners for same application
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant appoints two principal patent practitioners simultaneously, the applicant should indicate with whom correspondence is to be conducted; if not indicated and one is local to DC, correspondence will be conducted with the local practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a second principal practitioner is later appointed without revocation of the first, the correspondence address of the second practitioner is entered into the application so Office letters are sent to the later-named practitioner (Ex parte Eggan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph for Dual Correspondence (¶ 4.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: When double correspondence is attempted, include form paragraph 4.01 ('Dual Correspondence') in the Office action instructing the applicant to conduct future correspondence through the attorney/agent of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: the first time a reply is received directly from applicant, include paragraph 4.01 and send a copy of the action to the applicant. Subsequent actions and isolated instances may be handled differently; do not send copies of subsequent Office actions to the applicant if additional replies are filed.
